title: 2005 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: Alice and Bob play a game involving a circle whose circumference is divided by \(12\) equally-spaced points. The points are numbered clockwise, from \(1\) to \(12.\) Both start on point \(12.\) Alice moves clockwise and Bob, counterclockwise. In a turn of the game, Alice moves \(5\) points clockwise and Bob moves \(9\) points counterclockwise. The game ends when they stop on the same point. How many turns will this take?

solutions.text:
After one turn, Alice has moved \(5\) points clockwise and Bob has moved \(9\) points counterclockwise. Their relative movement is \(5+9=14\) points per turn.

They meet when \(14k\) is a multiple of \(12\), where \(k\) is the number of turns.

Since \(14k\equiv2k\pmod{12}\), the smallest positive \(k\) making \(2k\) a multiple of \(12\) is \(6\).

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Track the relative motion of Alice and Bob around the circle.
Together they close the gap by \(14\) points each turn, modulo \(12\).
